tasks.short: Lead the HR team, set daily priorities, and resolve staffing, pay and employee issues across our three sites.

today.trigger: Daily team coordination, an urgent manager request, or an issue escalated by an HR colleague.
steps: Read Teams and Outlook updates from HR colleagues and site managers.
Check vacancies, onboarding gaps, absence deadlines and payroll exceptions in the relevant systems.
Ask colleagues for missing facts, progress and capacity.
Set priorities, assign owners and resolve competing requests.
Coach colleagues, handle sensitive escalations and follow up on agreed actions.
drudgery: Chasing updates already recorded elsewhere
Rebuilding meeting agendas and action lists
Checking several systems for overdue work
Repeating the same status questions across three sites
today.time_sinks: Preparation and follow-up consume time around the conversations; interruptions and sensitive escalations remain substantial.

lenses.faster: A daily brief brings together overdue actions, deadlines and exceptions with source links. Manual status collection and agenda preparation largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Rules flag missing owners, approaching deadlines and overdue actions after a successful data refresh. Routine reminders follow agreed escalation rules.
lenses.ambitious: Review every site's route from vacancy to productive employee each week, including week-one onboarding and day-90 outcomes. Give more coaching to managers whose teams repeatedly encounter problems.
lenses.joy: Remove chasing, copying and meeting administration. Keep coaching, resolving difficult situations and helping colleagues succeed.
lenses.options: Compare alternative weekly priorities against team capacity and statutory deadlines. Show which work each option postpones.
lenses.altitude: Design the team's service standards, escalation rules and decision rights. Use exceptions to improve how HR works across the sites.
reach: HR Business Partner: prepare site service reviews and manager follow-up lists
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: specify operational exception reports
Recruiter and L&D Specialist: coordinate handovers from accepted offer to productive employee

tasks.human_edge: The director judges urgency, supports colleagues, challenges managers and handles conflict with the authority and trust of a person.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: software collects status and an llm_step drafts the brief, but directing and coaching the team remain human work. The whole task should stay assisted even if reminders run automatically.

in_practice.trigger: A successful nightly refresh prepares the morning brief; an explicitly recorded urgent escalation enters the queue immediately.
steps: Read authorised status fields and a shared action register; check refresh timestamps and missing data.
Apply approved rules for overdue actions, onboarding gaps, certificate deadlines and absence-process milestones.
Draft a short agenda with source links, owners, deadlines and unresolved questions.
Let the director set priorities, coach colleagues and decide sensitive escalations.
Record agreed actions and send routine reminders under the approved escalation rules.
in_practice.human_gate: The director decides priorities, assignments and employee-related actions. Restricted employee cases stay outside general team briefs; urgent cases use the live escalation route rather than waiting for Power BI.
systems: Existing AFAS extract and Power BI
Recruitee and Studytube through approved exports or verified interfaces
Teams, Outlook and a restricted SharePoint action register
Proposed workflow and approved language-model service
data_needed: Action owner, due date, status and escalation category
Vacancy and onboarding milestone status
Certificate validity and completion status
Authorised absence-process dates without diagnoses
Team availability and agreed service priorities
Source timestamps and access permissions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint action register containing source timestamps, rule alerts, director decisions, owners and reminder history; sensitive case records remain separately restricted.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors allow an administrator to define which records and fields an external application retrieves.
Studytube offers certificate-expiry notifications; availability and configuration at Noordhaven still need checking.
The proposed combined brief and estimates of 25% less director effort and 1.2 times faster completion are untested planning assumptions.

risks: A nightly dashboard can miss an urgent payroll or employee issue; every brief must display its data age.
Sensitive case details could leak through broad Teams access or inherited SharePoint permissions.

Reminders cannot establish that reintegration obligations were fulfilled; retain accountable owners and evidence under the Wet verbetering poortwachter. [UWV reintegration guidance](https://www.uwv.nl/nl/ziek/re-integratie/samenwerking-werknemer-werkgever)

Collecting status can become employee monitoring; assess applicable OR rights before introducing such a system. [AP guidance on personnel monitoring](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/ondernemingsraad/de-or-en-personeelsvolgsystemen)
research_questions: What share of the director's coordination time is status collection and follow-up rather than coaching or conflict resolution?
Can the existing systems expose reliable owner, deadline and completion fields without colleagues maintaining duplicate records?
Does a four-week pilot reduce total HR preparation time while preserving urgent escalation response times?
Which information may appear in a team brief, and which cases require separate permissions?

tasks.short: Help managers apply our policies fairly and propose changes when the rules or practice need fixing.

today.trigger: A manager asks about policy, an employee raises a concern, or a recurring issue exposes a policy gap.
steps: Clarify the question and obtain the necessary facts from the manager.
Find the current policy, applicable CAO and relevant guidance.
Check applicability, exceptions and previous approved interpretations.
Discuss sensitive facts with the HR Business Partner or legal adviser.
Advise the manager and draft any proposed policy change.
drudgery: Finding the approved version among several copies
Answering repeated procedural questions
Rewriting similar explanations for different managers
Checking whether a policy applies to warehouse, transport or office staff
today.time_sinks: Finding authoritative rules and reconstructing context slow routine answers; allegations, conflicting accounts and legal interpretation require careful discussion.

lenses.faster: Retrieve approved passages and draft a cited answer using the employee's applicable CAO and policy version. Searching folders and rewriting standard explanations largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's structured question starts retrieval and drafting, while missing facts or conflicting sources create an escalation. Sensitive allegations go directly to a named human contact.
lenses.ambitious: Give shift managers consistent procedural guidance at all three sites and identify recurring policy gaps. Test proposed wording against realistic warehouse, transport and office situations.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive searches and standard replies. Preserve fair conversations, difficult judgment and helping managers act responsibly.
lenses.options: Draft several policy approaches with practical consequences, implementation costs and questions for legal review. Separate required changes from choices Noordhaven can make.
lenses.altitude: Own a maintained policy service with clear applicability, approved interpretations and escalation routes. Improve rules using recurring questions and complaints.
reach: HR Business Partner: prepare routine manager guidance
HR Administrator: maintain policy applicability and version records
L&D Specialist: turn approved guidance into manager training examples

tasks.human_edge: Managers need contextual advice and a trusted person for discrimination, harassment, discipline and complaints; a fluent answer cannot assess credibility or determine fairness.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: an llm_step retrieves and drafts within a controlled workflow, and an authorised HR person approves each substantive answer. The earlier automate score fits routine preparation better than the full advisory task.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits a policy question through a restricted SharePoint intake.
steps: Check the question category and route complaints or sensitive employee matters to the designated human process.
Retrieve current approved policies, applicable CAO passages and effective dates.
Draft an answer with citations, missing facts and explicit limits on applicability.
Have the responsible HR reviewer approve or amend the advice; obtain legal review where needed.
Send the approved answer and record recurring questions as proposed policy improvements.
in_practice.human_gate: HR approves substantive guidance before release. Legal interpretation, complaints, sanctions and policy changes require the relevant human decision process, including applicable OR involvement.
systems: SharePoint policy library and restricted intake
AFAS Profit for minimum necessary applicability fields
Proposed retrieval service and approved language-model service
Power Automate if licensing and tenant configuration are confirmed
data_needed: Approved policies with owners, versions and effective dates
Current transport CAO and Noordhaven's warehouse CAO
Employee category and applicable contractual framework
Approved legal interpretations and escalation rules
Minimum necessary facts supplied by the manager
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint advice register containing the question, cited versions, draft, reviewer changes and approved response; complaint details remain in the designated confidential case record.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports SharePoint-triggered approval workflows and records approval outcomes; it is a proposed addition here.
Retrieval from a controlled policy library can support checkable drafts, but citations and applicability still require review.
The estimates of 50% less director effort and 1.6 times faster approved advice assume many repeated procedural questions and are untested.

risks: An outdated policy, wrong CAO or invented exception could produce unfair advice; absent authoritative support must trigger escalation.
A complaint could be mishandled as an ordinary policy question, delaying confidential human support.

Applicable personnel-policy changes can require OR consent, subject to matters already substantively regulated by a CAO. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/faq/personeelsregelingen)

If the system begins evaluating workers or recommending employment decisions, assess its EU AI Act classification and applicable obligations before expanding use. [European Commission AI Act guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
research_questions: What proportion of manager questions can be answered from approved sources without investigating disputed facts?
Are the two CAOs and all policies versioned with clear applicability and an accountable owner?
In a reviewed test set, does the system cite the correct rule and escalate every sensitive or unsupported question?
Does drafting reduce total HR handling time after corrections and legal review are counted?

tasks.short: Use HR figures to understand hiring, retention and absence problems, then recommend changes that managers can act on.

today.trigger: A monthly review, deteriorating HR metric, or request to explain a site or workforce problem.
steps: Review Power BI reports and request supporting extracts from the analyst.
Reconcile definitions and compare sites, roles, shifts and hiring cohorts.
Gather manager explanations and relevant process information.
Assess possible causes and develop recommendations.
Present findings and agree actions and follow-up measures.
systems: Power BI and nightly AFAS extract
drudgery: Reconciling headcount and metric definitions
Recreating the same comparisons each month
Explaining dashboard movements in slides
Chasing missing onboarding and day-90 records
today.time_sinks: Data reconciliation and report preparation take time; distinguishing a genuine cause from seasonality, workforce mix or recording differences is harder.

lenses.faster: Calculate agreed metrics and cohort comparisons automatically, then draft commentary from validated results. Repeated reconciliation, chart building and slide preparation shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A successful refresh runs data-quality checks and flags material changes using approved thresholds. Failures produce a data exception rather than a confident explanation.
lenses.ambitious: Follow vacancies through acceptance, week-one onboarding, demonstrated productivity and day-90 retention. Test targeted improvements and measure whether they improve the North Star.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet repair and recurring report assembly. Keep investigating with managers and learning which interventions work.
lenses.options: Present competing explanations with supporting evidence and proposed tests. Compare interventions by expected benefit, cost and strength of evidence.
lenses.altitude: Own the measurement definitions and improvement programme. Require evidence that changes improve outcomes rather than merely move a dashboard number.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: define recurring analytical questions and report requirements
HR Business Partner: prepare site diagnostic packs
FP&A Analyst: connect hiring and retention improvements to labour-cost scenarios

tasks.human_edge: The director challenges explanations, understands site conditions and chooses fair interventions; observational patterns alone do not establish causes.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic_software calculates metrics, an llm_step drafts a sourced interpretation, and the director approves conclusions and interventions. Automating report production does not automate causal judgment.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly data refresh passes validation, or a scheduled monthly analysis is due.
steps: Join minimum necessary records using controlled vacancy, hire and employee identifiers; validate counts and refresh dates.
Calculate agreed metrics, flag incomplete cohorts and suppress groups below the approved disclosure threshold.
Compare outcomes by site, role and cohort with uncertainty and workforce-mix differences shown.
Draft an evidence pack separating observed facts, hypotheses and missing information.
Have the director and site managers select an intervention and record how its outcome will be assessed.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates the calculations; the director approves interpretations and interventions. The workflow produces group-level evidence and does not automatically score or sanction individuals.
systems: Power BI and existing AFAS extract
Recruitee through its authorised API or exports
Studytube through an approved data route
Excel or SharePoint for validated operational productivity milestones
Proposed calculation checks and approved language-model service
data_needed: Agreed metric definitions, denominators and reporting windows
Vacancy-to-hire links, pipeline dates and offer outcomes
Employee start dates, site, role, contracted hours and employment status
Week-one onboarding completion and role-specific productivity sign-off
Authorised absence totals without diagnoses
Agency-worker records kept distinct from employee cohorts
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint analysis register linked to versioned Power BI measures, extract timestamps, validation results, hypotheses, decisions and intervention outcomes.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh and refresh-history checks, providing a basis for repeatable reporting.
Recruitee documents an authenticated API that can support controlled integration; required reporting fields still need checking.
The combined vacancy-to-day-90 analysis and estimates of 55% less director effort and 1.8 times faster completion are untested.

risks: Missing vacancy links or productivity sign-offs could turn the North Star into a simple retention measure; report unfilled vacancies and missing outcomes explicitly.
Seasonality, role mix and small cohorts can create misleading comparisons and unsupported causal claims.

Absence analysis must exclude diagnoses and other prohibited medical details; small groups can still identify people. [AP guidance for employers](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers)
Individual performance or turnover scoring would need a separate privacy, OR and EU AI Act assessment; aggregate reporting is not permission to expand into employee profiling.
research_questions: Can a sample of vacancies be traced reliably through hire, week-one onboarding, productivity sign-off and day-90 employment status?
Do the director, Operations and analyst agree a vacancy-cohort denominator that does not hide unfilled roles or immature outcomes?
Can a historical replay distinguish meaningful changes from ordinary seasonal variation without excessive alerts?
Do pilot recommendations survive manager fact-checking and improve outcomes in a prospectively defined test?

tasks.short: Set and steer our hiring, learning and employee-relations programmes across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: Quarterly planning, a seasonal peak, a policy change, or an HR programme falling behind.
steps: Gather site priorities, workforce needs and programme results.
Review hiring capacity, mandatory training and employee-relations commitments.
Set programme goals, milestones, budgets and responsibilities.
Coordinate with Operations, Finance, HR specialists and the works council where relevant.
Review progress and adjust the programme when conditions change.
drudgery: Combining separate programme plans
Refreshing milestone presentations
Chasing dependencies between recruiters, administrators and trainers
Finding out too late that a site cannot release people for training
today.time_sinks: Building a coherent programme from separate plans and checking dependencies consume preparation time; negotiation over resources and priorities remains human.

lenses.faster: Build the programme review from shared milestones, capacity and exceptions. Repeated consolidation and presentation updates largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Changed milestones or capacity inputs trigger dependency checks and draft recovery plans. Owners receive approved reminders and unresolved conflicts reach the director.
lenses.ambitious: Plan onboarding and required training before recruitment campaigns start. Test whether all three sites can make new hires productive during peak periods.
lenses.joy: Remove programme administration and status chasing. Keep setting direction, building support and solving constraints with Operations.
lenses.options: Compare faster hiring, stronger internal development and different training schedules. Show costs, capacity limits and consequences for productive day-90 hires.
lenses.altitude: Design and improve the company's HR programmes as connected value streams. Set standards for handovers, results and escalation.
reach: L&D Specialist: coordinate site training capacity with hiring plans
Recruiter: align campaigns with onboarding capacity
Operations manager: co-design workforce readiness for seasonal peaks

tasks.human_edge: The director negotiates priorities, secures manager commitment and maintains constructive labour relations; programme execution depends on people accepting the plan.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: deterministic dependency checks and drafted plans support the director, who leads resource allocation and stakeholder negotiation. This concerns programme design rather than the daily supervision in task 991.

in_practice.trigger: A quarterly planning cycle starts, or an approved programme input or milestone materially changes.
steps: Collect current programme milestones, hiring plans, training capacity and approved budget limits.
Check dependencies, including trainer availability, shift release time and certificate requirements.
Draft programme scenarios with owners, milestones, costs and unresolved decisions.
Have the director agree the plan with Operations, Finance and relevant employee representatives.
Track the approved milestones and prepare exception-based progress reviews.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves programme priorities and resource changes. Complete the applicable OR process before implementing affected personnel arrangements; certificate or readiness requirements cannot be waived by a generated plan.
systems: Proposed planning checks and approved language-model service
data_needed: Hiring targets and start-date scenarios by site and role
Training requirements, session capacity and certificate validity
Operational release-time constraints for each shift
Programme owners, dependencies and milestone status
Approved budget and consultation requirements
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint programme register containing input versions, scenarios, approved milestones, consultation records and reasons for plan changes.

evidence.claim: Studytube provides compliance tracking and certificate-expiry notifications, which can inform training programme exceptions.
Shared milestone data and deterministic dependency checks can reduce repeated programme consolidation.
The proposed integrated programme workflow and estimates of 35% less director effort and 1.4 times faster completion are untested.

risks: An apparently feasible programme may ignore operational shift coverage, training release time or limited trainer capacity.
Course completion alone may not demonstrate practical competence or readiness for the assigned work.
Training-policy changes can fall under OR consent rights, subject to the CAO context. [SER personnel-arrangements guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/faq/personeelsregelingen)
Excessive programme alerts could add work for the single HRIS analyst and specialist owners instead of reducing total effort.
research_questions: Are programme dependencies and operational release-time constraints recorded well enough to check automatically?
Does a peak-season replay identify the bottlenecks that actually delayed productive starts?
Can specialist owners maintain one shared plan without duplicate updates?
Does the pilot reduce total planning effort while improving week-one onboarding and certificate readiness?

tasks.short: Prepare the HR operating budget, explain spending differences and agree changes with Finance.

today.trigger: Annual budgeting, a monthly finance review, or a material change in HR spending.
steps: Collect AFAS actuals, commitments and prior budget figures.
Ask HR specialists for recruitment, learning, advisory and system spending plans.
Build the budget and forecast in Excel using agreed assumptions.
Discuss differences and funding choices with Finance.
Monitor actual spending and agree corrective actions.
systems: AFAS Profit general ledger and accounts payable
drudgery: Copying actuals into budget workbooks
Reconciling inconsistent cost categories
Chasing commitment and forecast updates
Drafting recurring variance commentary
today.time_sinks: Reconciling actuals and collecting assumptions consume preparation time; agreeing spending priorities requires the director and Finance.

lenses.faster: Refresh mapped actuals and commitments automatically and draft explanations for checked variances. Copying, formula repair and recurring commentary shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A closed finance period triggers a reconciled budget pack and flags missing assumptions or material differences. Spending decisions remain within existing approval limits.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling HR forecast linked to hiring volume, onboarding capacity and productive day-90 hires. Review which spending produces useful outcomes.
lenses.joy: Remove workbook maintenance and repeated reconciliation. Keep choosing investments and discussing their value with Finance.
lenses.options: Compare recruitment, retention and learning spending scenarios with clear assumptions. Show the budget effect and uncertainty rather than a single precise forecast.
lenses.altitude: Own the investment rules and outcome measures for HR spending. Challenge the assumptions behind requests instead of assembling every budget line.
reach: Controller: prepare HR cost-centre variance explanations
FP&A Analyst: develop HR investment scenarios
L&D and Recruitment specialists: consolidate programme spending forecasts

tasks.human_edge: The director weighs service quality, employee outcomes and commercial constraints, and negotiates credible commitments with Finance.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic_software calculates and reconciles the budget, an llm_step drafts commentary, and humans approve assumptions and funding. Payroll totals and agency costs enter only where they belong in the agreed budget scope.

in_practice.trigger: Finance marks the monthly period closed, or the annual budget cycle opens.
steps: Load closed-period actuals, approved commitments and the controlled account-to-budget mapping.
Reconcile totals with the Controller and flag uncoded or unexplained entries.
Calculate the forecast and scenarios from explicitly entered assumptions.
Draft variance explanations tied to ledger lines and assumption changes.
Have the director and Finance approve the forecast and resulting spending actions.
in_practice.human_gate: The Controller confirms reconciliation; the director and authorised Finance approver agree assumptions and budget changes. The workflow does not release payments or modify payroll.
systems: AFAS Profit general ledger and accounts payable
Proposed calculation checks and approved language-model service
data_needed: Closed-period HR cost-centre actuals and account mapping
Approved budget, purchase commitments and relevant contracts
Recruitment, training, advisory and system spending drivers
Finance-approved treatment of payroll, agency labour, VAT and accruals
Approval limits and forecast owners
in_practice.logs_to: Finance-controlled SharePoint budget archive containing reconciliations, model versions, assumptions, draft commentary and approval records.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors support controlled retrieval of configured data fields; suitable finance definitions must be configured and verified.
A deterministic budget model can calculate scenarios while a language model drafts explanations from reconciled results.
The estimates of 45% less director effort and 1.6 times faster approved budget preparation are untested and exclude faster finance-close completion.

risks: Incorrect account mapping or accrual treatment could produce convincing but wrong variance explanations.
Agency labour and payroll could be counted twice if HR and Operations budget boundaries are unclear.
Apparent savings may reduce onboarding quality or move costs into overtime, agency use or early turnover.
Detailed payroll or contract data could reach an unnecessarily broad model context; calculate with restricted data and draft from approved summaries.
research_questions: Which costs belong to the director's personnel-operations budget, and which remain with Operations or Finance?
Can actuals and commitments reconcile to the Controller's figures without recurring manual adjustments?
Does the model reproduce a prior approved budget and explain its major variances correctly?
After review and corrections, does the pilot reduce combined HR and Finance handling time?

tasks.short: Track changes in Dutch employment rules and our CAOs, and decide what Noordhaven needs to change.

today.trigger: A scheduled legal update, a published ruling, a CAO amendment, or a question about an emerging obligation.
steps: Read official updates, sector material, rulings and legal-adviser briefings.
Compare changes with the current transport and warehouse CAOs and Noordhaven policies.
Assess applicability, effective dates and operational consequences.
Ask the legal adviser about unclear or disputed interpretations.
Brief the relevant HR specialists and managers and assign follow-up actions.
drudgery: Checking several sources for changes
Reading long documents to find a few relevant passages
Comparing versions manually
Rewriting updates for different HR specialists
today.time_sinks: Finding and comparing relevant material consumes reading time; assessing legal status and company applicability requires expertise.

lenses.faster: Monitor approved sources, compare versions and draft an impact note with exact passages. Repeated website checks and most first-pass reading disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A detected source change creates a draft update and review task. Missing access, conflicting dates or unclear legal status generate an exception.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a live map from employment obligations to policies, payroll rules, training and responsible owners. Check implementation after each relevant change.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive scanning and document comparison. Keep interpreting consequential changes and helping the business prepare.
lenses.options: Compare implementation approaches within the confirmed legal and CAO boundaries. Show unresolved legal questions before comparing costs or timing.
lenses.altitude: Design and audit the process that turns authoritative changes into implemented controls. Review coverage and unresolved obligations rather than every source document.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: prepare CAO change summaries
Payroll Specialist: identify provisions requiring payroll-rule review
HR Administrator and L&D Specialist: prepare policy and training update lists

tasks.human_edge: The director and legal adviser distinguish proposals from binding rules, interpret applicability and accept responsibility for implementation decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic_software detects changes, an llm_step extracts cited provisions and drafts their possible impact, and an authorised reviewer approves interpretation and action. Automatic monitoring does not make the output legal advice.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled checks detect a change in an approved source, or an authorised owner uploads a new CAO or adviser briefing.
steps: Retrieve the changed document and record its publisher, publication date, legal status and version.
Compare relevant passages with the previous version and extract effective dates and affected subjects.
Map possible impacts to the applicable CAO, policy, payroll rule or HR process.
Have the director and legal adviser confirm applicability and approve the action list.
Assign owners and retain evidence that approved changes were implemented.
in_practice.human_gate: A qualified reviewer confirms legal status, applicability and interpretation before guidance or configuration changes are approved. Neither CAO bargaining nor OR procedures can be completed by approving an AI summary.
systems: Approved official, sector and adviser sources
data_needed: Approved source list and lawful access arrangements
Current and previous transport CAO versions
Noordhaven's current and previous warehouse CAO versions
Company applicability notes and approved legal interpretations
Policy, payroll-rule and process-owner mapping
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint obligation register containing source snapshots, passage comparisons, legal-review decisions, owners, deadlines and implementation evidence.

evidence.claim: Version comparison and structured extraction can reduce first-pass reading while leaving legal interpretation with a reviewer.
The proposed monitoring-to-implementation workflow is a design for Noordhaven, with no documented company deployment.
The estimates of 60% less director effort and twice-faster reviewed impact notes are untested; statutory implementation periods are unchanged.

risks: A proposal, political agreement or non-applicable ruling could be presented as a binding obligation; retain source status and obtain legal confirmation.
Monitoring can miss an important amendment if a source changes format or access fails; audit coverage against independent adviser updates.
The fictional warehouse CAO has not been supplied, so its provisions and relationship to other rules cannot be inferred.

EU AI Act classifications and application dates require current verification for the intended use; avoid relying on a stored summary. [European Commission AI Act guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
research_questions: Which sources provide adequate coverage of Noordhaven's obligations, and can they be monitored lawfully and reliably?
In a historical test, does the workflow detect every material change identified by the legal adviser?
Can reviewers trace every impact statement to an exact passage and distinguish proposals, rulings and binding provisions?
Do approved updates reach the correct policy and system owners, with verifiable implementation?

tasks.short: Check that jobs are described and graded consistently under the applicable CAO and our agreed evaluation method.

today.trigger: A new job, changed duties, grading dispute, or scheduled review of job classifications.
steps: Collect the job description, actual duties and applicable evaluation method.
Ask the manager and job holders to clarify responsibilities and working conditions.
Compare the job with reference functions and previously evaluated roles.
Review the proposed classification with the Compensation and Benefits Specialist.
Approve the outcome through the agreed process and communicate the rationale and appeal route.
systems: SharePoint job descriptions and evaluation records
AFAS Profit job and salary structures
drudgery: Comparing inconsistent job-description formats
Finding previous evaluation rationales
Building evidence tables manually
Checking whether changed wording reflects changed duties
today.time_sinks: Document comparison and missing evidence delay preparation; agreeing actual job content and resolving contested classifications require human involvement.

lenses.faster: Convert descriptions into a common evidence format and retrieve relevant reference functions and earlier rationales. Manual comparison and missing-information lists shrink.
lenses.autonomous: An approved new or changed job description triggers an evidence-completeness check and a draft comparison pack. It does not trigger a grade or pay change.
lenses.ambitious: Review similar jobs across all three sites for inconsistent descriptions or classifications. Detect role drift before it becomes a dispute.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repetitive comparison tables. Keep understanding jobs and reaching fair, explainable outcomes.
lenses.options: Show plausible reference-function matches with supporting passages, differences and unanswered questions. Compare outcomes only within the agreed method.
lenses.altitude: Own the integrity of the job-evaluation process, reviewer consistency and appeals. Audit the method's application rather than rewrite every assessment.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: prepare evaluation evidence packs
HR Business Partner: organise structured job-content clarification
HR Administrator: maintain approved job-description and classification versions

tasks.human_edge: A trained evaluator establishes the real job content and applies the agreed method; the director handles fairness, consistency and contested decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: an llm_step structures descriptions and drafts comparisons, while trained humans evaluate jobs. Deterministic scoring is appropriate only for explicit, authorised rules after the underlying evidence is confirmed.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits a new or materially changed job description for evaluation.
steps: Confirm the applicable CAO, evaluation method and approved reference-function version.
Extract duties and responsibilities into the method's evidence template, citing the source text.
Flag missing information and compare the job with relevant references and internal precedents.
Have a trained evaluator verify job content with the manager and job holders and propose a classification.
Complete approval and appeal procedures before an administrator records the authorised result in AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: Trained evaluators and the authorised approval process decide the classification. Changes to the evaluation system follow applicable CAO and OR procedures; no automated pay or grade writes occur.
systems: Applicable CAO and approved reference-function documents
Proposed retrieval and approved language-model service
data_needed: Current job duties and confirmed responsibilities
Applicable CAO and agreed evaluation method
Approved reference functions and method definitions
Previous evaluation rationales and appeal outcomes
Version history showing substantive job changes
Job-content evidence without unnecessary job-holder personal details
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint evaluation record containing cited evidence, questions, reviewer corrections, approved rationale and appeal information; AFAS holds the authorised classification.

evidence.claim: Structured extraction and retrieval can prepare job-comparison evidence, but consistent grading requires an agreed method and trained reviewers.
The proposed comparison assistant and estimates of 35% less director effort and 1.4 times faster completed reviews are untested.

risks: AI could impose a generic points system instead of the applicable sector or warehouse method; use the actual approved scheme. [STL reference-function guidance](https://www.stl.nl/werkgevers/cao-en-functiewaardering/functietypering/)
Old internal classifications may preserve historical undervaluation; precedent is evidence to inspect rather than automatic ground truth.
Polished descriptions can overstate duties or omit physical demands and shift responsibilities; confirm actual work with people who know the job.

If AI outputs influence individual promotion or employment terms, assess the intended use under the EU AI Act; a human approval gate alone does not settle classification. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
research_questions: Which evaluation method applies to each employee group, and are its authorised references and appeal procedures available?
Can the assistant reproduce reviewers' evidence extraction without inventing responsibilities or omitting material demands?
Do trained reviewers agree more consistently when using the comparison pack?
Does the pilot save preparation time without increasing contested decisions or appeal corrections?

tasks.short: Forecast the people and skills each site needs, including recruitment, internal moves and seasonal agency workers.

today.trigger: Annual workforce planning, a seasonal peak forecast, or a significant change in expected operational demand.
steps: Obtain expected volumes and staffing requirements from Operations.
Review current headcount, contracted hours, vacancies, departures and absence assumptions.
Check agency capacity and required skills and certificates.
Build site-level staffing scenarios in Excel with hiring and training lead times.
Agree recruitment, development and flex-worker plans with Operations and Finance.
drudgery: Combining employee and agency figures from different sources
Rebuilding staffing scenarios
Reconciling headcount, FTE and usable hours
Checking whether planned starts have enough onboarding and training capacity
today.time_sinks: Preparing compatible inputs and rebuilding scenarios take time; agreeing demand assumptions and workable staffing responses requires Operations and Finance.

lenses.faster: Refresh supply inputs and calculate workforce scenarios with explicit formulas. Repeated merging, spreadsheet rebuilding and narrative preparation largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved demand revision or validated supply refresh recalculates gaps and produces a draft action plan. Missing inputs or breached constraints stop publication.
lenses.ambitious: Run a rolling forecast by site, shift and skill before each peak. Include time to productivity and day-90 retention so planned hires translate into usable capacity.
lenses.joy: Remove consolidation and formula maintenance. Keep working with Operations on credible plans and better workforce resilience.
lenses.options: Compare permanent hiring, internal development, agency capacity and lawful overtime assumptions under low, base and high demand. Show costs, lead times and failure points.
lenses.altitude: Own the workforce-planning assumptions, forecast accuracy and response rules. Improve the planning system rather than repeatedly construct the forecast.
reach: FP&A Analyst: prepare labour-supply and cost scenarios
Recruiter: translate staffing gaps into recruitment timing
L&D Specialist: translate skill gaps into development demand
Operations planner: co-develop aggregate capacity assumptions

tasks.human_edge: The director challenges optimistic assumptions and negotiates feasible workforce commitments; Operations confirms demand and practical capacity.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic_software calculates demand and supply scenarios, an llm_step drafts explanations, and humans approve assumptions and actions. Aggregate capacity planning is separate from allocating named workers to shifts.

in_practice.trigger: Operations approves a revised demand file, or a scheduled planning refresh has complete validated inputs.
steps: Load approved operational demand, employee supply, agency hours and skill-readiness inputs.
Reconcile headcount, contracted hours and usable hours, keeping employee and agency populations distinct.
Calculate low, base and high scenarios using confirmed productivity, availability and ramp-up assumptions.
Identify staffing and skill gaps with recruitment, training, agency-capacity and applicable working-time constraints.
Have the director, Operations and Finance approve the assumptions and action plan before orders or hiring commitments are made.
Compare forecast capacity with actual outcomes and record assumption changes.
in_practice.human_gate: Operations approves demand and productivity assumptions; HR and Finance approve the workforce response and cost. Hiring commitments, agency orders and material organisational changes use their existing authorisation and consultation processes.
systems: AFAS Profit extract and Power BI
Staffing agency portals through verified exports or interfaces
Excel or SharePoint demand files supplied by Operations
Proposed deterministic forecasting service and approved language-model service
data_needed: Operational volume forecasts and validated labour-hours assumptions by site, shift and skill
Contracted hours, planned departures and approved aggregate availability assumptions
Recruitment pipeline, expected starts and realistic hiring lead times
Productivity ramp-up and day-90 retention assumptions by role and cohort
Skill requirements, certificate validity and training capacity
Agency capacity, rates and applicable CAO and working-time constraints
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint workforce-plan archive containing input timestamps, model versions, assumptions, scenario outputs, approvals and forecast-versus-actual reviews.

evidence.claim: AFAS and Recruitee provide documented data interfaces that can support employee-supply and recruitment inputs; field availability requires verification.
Explicit demand-and-supply formulas can generate checkable scenarios without using a language model for numerical forecasting.
The combined forecasting workflow and estimates of 50% less director effort and 1.7 times faster approved plans are untested.

risks: Operational demand and productivity inputs are not in the supplied HR systems; a forecast cannot infer them reliably from headcount.
Employee and agency records may overlap, while headcount may conceal contracted-hour and skill differences.
Hires may be treated as immediately productive despite onboarding, certification and early turnover.
Aggregate absence assumptions must not become individual medical predictions or employee scoring.
A staffing scenario may overlook CAO or working-time constraints; confirm them before approving overtime or structural workforce changes.
research_questions: Can Operations provide validated demand-to-labour assumptions by site, shift and required skill?
Can employee and agency usable hours be reconciled across AFAS and all three portals without double counting?
Does a historical replay outperform the current forecast on capacity gaps and timing while showing uncertainty honestly?
Do proposed actions remain feasible after recruitment lead times, training capacity, CAO constraints and agency availability are checked?

role.altitude: The HR Director becomes the owner of workforce outcomes and the systems that produce them: clear policies, reliable handovers, useful measurement, effective programmes and accountable decisions.
reach: Prepare site diagnostic and service-review packs currently assembled by HR Business Partners
Specify repeatable analyses and data-quality rules with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Develop HR cost and workforce scenarios with the Controller and FP&A team
Coordinate recruitment, onboarding and learning capacity across specialist roles
Prepare policy, CAO and job-evaluation evidence for specialists and legal reviewers
role.ceiling_note: The current steps and anatomy are inferred from the supplied context. Savings estimate steady-state director effort after routine review and rework; speedups estimate elapsed completion of the same task, including its human gates. Both require pilots and exclude initial implementation costs. Applied to the supplied hours, the estimates release about 560 hours a year: 41% of the 1,364 listed hours, or 35% of an implied 1,600-hour role. The remaining 236 annual hours are unassessed. At EUR 110/hour this is about EUR 61,600 of capacity value, not cash savings. Avoid double counting daily supervision and programme planning, and count work transferred to colleagues. Trust, coaching, disputes, negotiations, legal accountability and consultation periods limit further gains; the single HRIS analyst also limits how many workflows can be built and maintained.
skills_to_grow: Define vacancy-cohort metrics, productivity milestones and reliable day-90 outcomes
Distinguish descriptive patterns from causal evidence and design practical intervention tests
Write explicit workflow rules, exceptions, decision rights and approval gates
Evaluate workforce scenarios, forecast uncertainty and investment trade-offs with Finance and Operations
Maintain CAO applicability, policy versions and effective legal-review processes
Apply AVG data minimisation, access controls, OR requirements and use-specific EU AI Act assessments
Coach shift managers, negotiate priorities and handle sensitive employee relations
role.ambitious_version: Run a continuous improvement programme for hire to productive across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Connect approved vacancies, offers, week-one onboarding, demonstrated role-specific productivity and day-90 retention, while keeping unfilled vacancies and missing outcomes visible. Use validated forecasts to prepare hiring and training capacity before peaks, test improvements with site managers, and redirect released time toward manager capability, employee trust and interventions that produce more successful hires.
